changes.after: Choose whether a function returns one hidden type or different allowed types.

before: An opaque result written some Protocol hides one concrete result type from callers. An existential written any Protocol can hold different conforming concrete types. Neither means that the value has no concrete type.

makeTrail always returns Trail behind some Captioned. The caller can invoke the promised caption() requirement, which takes no arguments and returns text. chooseCaption uses any Captioned to return either Harbor or Trail; the Bool selects the stored concrete value. Trail() and Harbor() create empty value instances. This lesson concerns some in result position, not some parameters or SwiftUI result builders. Existential storage is often called boxing; this does not promise a particular allocation or performance cost.
Optional practice: Keep makeTrail opaque and make chooseCaption select the correct caption. Predict a different input before running.
after: Captioned promises a caption() method that returns text. A function can describe its answer using this promise without naming its exact type. some and any give that promise different rules.
A result written some Captioned hides one fixed type from callers. makeTrail always returns Trail. The caller can still use caption(), because that ability is promised.
A result written any Captioned can hold different types that meet the promise. chooseCaption returns Harbor when water is true and Trail otherwise. Each returned value still has its own actual type.

For an ordinary function returning some Captioned, every return path must use the same actual type. Returning Trail on one path and Harbor on another fails that rule. This lesson is about function results; SwiftUI's special view-building rules come later.
Keep some Captioned for makeTrail and return Trail. Use any Captioned for chooseCaption. Select Harbor for true and Trail for false, keeping each type's own caption.
